:::{#thm-fisher-kl-curvature}
#### The expected information is the curvature of the Kullback--Leibler divergence

Under the assumptions of @thm-score-mean-zero,
let $\param_0$ be the true value of the scalar parameter $\param$,
and let $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\param)$ be the Kullback--Leibler divergence
of the model with parameter $\param$ from the model with parameter $\param_0$
(@exr-fisher-kl-curvature).
Then $D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ has a minimum of $0$ at $\param_0$,
with zero slope there,
and its second derivative at $\param_0$ is the [expected information](#def-einf):

$$D_{\mathrm{KL}}''(\param_0) = \einf(\param_0)$$

:::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-fisher-kl-curvature, worked in @sol-fisher-kl-curvature.
It builds on @thm-score-mean-zero.

:::
